argument_summary: The certification defense should be narrowed rather than treated as clean compliance. The admissible record supports that aggregate readiness passed and rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, and it supports a deployment posture based on documented limitations and monitoring. It does not support the stronger claim that the Spanish-language billing support gap is non-material merely because it is low-volume or localized. On this record, the most supportable position is that certification can be defended only with an explicit caveat that the named-use-case limitation remains unresolved under policy unless disclosed or covered by approved risk acceptance.
claims_about_policy: Policy cuts against a clean compliance finding here: a weakness is material when it affects a named launch use case, and product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when customer commitments name the affected segment or legal review is still pending. Public governance guidance on documenting limitations and monitoring risk supports a controlled-deployment framing, but it does not replace the internal requirement to disclose, resolve, or obtain approved risk acceptance for a material limitation. The defensible interpretation is therefore caveated compliance at most, not full policy satisfaction.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation has a real launch-path cost because it can delay the international pilot path, but that cost does not cure the policy gap. It is relevant only to whether the auditor treats this as requiring immediate escalation versus allowing a bounded caveat and continued monitoring while preserving launch velocity.
concessions: The current record does not show that the Spanish-language billing support limitation was disclosed in required launch documentation.
The current record does not show approved risk acceptance for this named launch use case.
The open legal review means a policy-relevant predicate remains unresolved.
The low-volume characterization is not enough, on its own, to defeat materiality under the stated policy.
